output.review_comment:
Two of the changes are correct: the ValueError for negative quantities and the off-by-one fix ((top - first + 1), because ranges include both ends). With those alone, every test except test_bulk_order passes using normal graduated pricing.

The "volume pricing" branch should be removed. It exists only to make test_bulk_order pass, and it contradicts the docstring, which says "reaching a higher tier never changes the price of the units in the lower tiers." It also creates a big price cliff: 500 units costs 105,000 cents but 501 units costs 75,150. Wholesale has the same problem: 50 units costs 46,000 but 51 costs 40,800. Buying more should never make an order cheaper, and this invites exploitation and billing disputes.

test_bulk_order disagrees with both the docstring and the other STANDARD_TIERS tests, which all assume graduated pricing (graduated gives 120,000 for 600 units, not 90,000). Escalate this to the teammate or pricing team instead of hard-coding a special case: either the test's expected value is wrong or the pricing model is changing, and a person needs to decide which. Please keep the two correct fixes, drop the last-tier shortcut, and leave that one test failing with a note asking for a decision. Credit for disclosing the conflict in the PR description, but it shouldn't merge as written.
